what: A pinion pushes a guided rack, turning motor rotation into straight travel. A rack and pinion turns rotation into lift: measure height per motor turn.
try: Reset and run the supplied out-and-back program.
Count motor turns and compare them with rack travel.
Stop the program and use a low manual speed to approach a travel stop.
why: At the gear’s pitch circle, tangential distance becomes rack displacement. The guide prevents unwanted sideways motion. At a physical stop the mechanism stalls instead of moving through the end of the rail.
matters: Rack drives appear in lifting equipment, machine slides and steering.
question: If the pinion turns twice as far, what happens before reaching the stop?
answer: The ideal rack travel doubles. A stop limits the actual travel, so encoder rotation alone is not enough evidence.
further: Compare lifting against gravity with a horizontal shuttle.
Explain why a larger pinion gives more travel per turn but less force for the same torque.
formula: travel = pitch radius × angle in radians;  8T pinion: r = 4 mm
